_how: First-run questionnaire. Ask each round with ONE AskUserQuestion call (max 4 questions per call, 2-4 options each; 'Other' is added automatically). Before asking, pre-select the option the project itself suggests and put it first with '(Recommended)'. Store answers in <videos>/video.config.json → answers[key]. To extend: add a question (new key) or an option, then bump `version` — projects with an older questionsVersion get asked ONLY the new keys.

questions.question: What are these videos mainly for?

options.label: Tutorials by role
options.description: A series per user type (e.g. member, admin): how to use every part of the product.

options.label: Product explainer
options.description: One or a few videos: what the product is, why it matters, how it works. Good for the homepage and ads.

options.label: Feature walkthroughs
options.description: One short video per feature or release, shipped as features land.

options.label: In-app onboarding
options.description: Short clips embedded in the product's own screens and empty states.

options.label: End users / customers
options.description: People using the product day to day. Plain words, no jargon.

options.label: Staff / admins
options.description: Internal team running the product. Can be more detailed; may be unlisted.

options.label: Prospects / investors
options.description: People deciding whether to use or back it. Outcome-led, persuasive.

options.label: Developers
options.description: Technical audience: APIs, setup, integration.

questions.question: Which shape should the videos be?

options.label: Landscape 16:9
options.description: YouTube, websites, presentations. 1920×1080.

options.label: Vertical 9:16
options.description: Shorts, Reels, TikTok, WhatsApp status. 1080×1920.

options.label: Both
options.description: Landscape main videos plus vertical cut-downs of the key moments.

options.label: Square 1:1
options.description: Feeds (LinkedIn, Instagram, X). 1080×1080.

questions.question: How long should each video be?

options.label: 60–90 seconds
options.description: One topic per video. Best for tutorials and retention.

options.label: Under 45 seconds
options.description: Snackable: Shorts, ads, in-app tips.

options.label: 2–4 minutes
options.description: Deeper walkthroughs that cover a full flow end to end.

options.label: Motion explainer
options.description: Animated scenes, 3D icons, kinetic text and app screens in device frames, with a voice-over. The proven default.

options.label: Screen tour
options.description: Real product screens with a cursor, zooms and spotlights on each button. Best for 'how do I…' tutorials.

options.label: Animated presenter
options.description: A cartoon host stands beside the content, lip-syncs to the voice and points at what it explains.

options.label: Real person / AI avatar
options.description: You (recorded on camera) or an AI avatar (HeyGen / D-ID) talks in a bubble or side panel over the screens.

questions.question: What should appear on screen? (pick all that fit)

options.label: Real app screens
options.description: Captured from the running product, signed in as the right role. Always matches the narration.

options.label: 3D icons + motion
options.description: Animated concept scenes: cards, counters, checklists, flows.

options.label: Stock / own footage
options.description: Real-world clips (free Pexels/Pixabay stock with a free key, or your own footage) for hooks and emotion.

options.label: Photos
options.description: Your own photos (team, events, customers) as montages and backgrounds.

options.label: Energetic
options.description: Faster voice (+8–12%), punchy transitions, sound effects on every beat.

options.label: Calm & clear
options.description: Natural pace, soft fades, light sound design. Good for finance, health, B2B.

options.label: Playful
options.description: Bouncy motion, bright colour pops, jokes allowed. Good for young audiences.

options.label: Word highlight
options.description: Short caption pages, the spoken word lights up in the brand colour (most watched on mute).

options.label: Subtle
options.description: Plain white captions, no highlight.

options.label: None
options.description: No burned-in captions (upload an .srt to YouTube instead).

questions.question: Who does the voice-over? (type "No voice" under Other for music + on-screen text only)

options.label: Free neural voices (no key)
options.description: Microsoft Edge neural voices through the open-source edge-tts tool: no account, no key, the same voices as Azure (needs Python). Word-timed captions included.

options.label: Azure Speech (free tier key)
options.description: Official Azure neural voices; the free F0 tier (0.5M chars/month) is enough. Needs AZURE_SPEECH_KEY + AZURE_SPEECH_REGION.

options.label: ElevenLabs
options.description: Most natural and expressive; paid; needs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY.

options.label: My own voice
options.description: You record each line (phone is fine); timings come from a transcription.

questions.question: Which accent / language should the voices have?

options.label: American English
options.description: e.g. en-US-AndrewMultilingualNeural / AvaMultilingualNeural.

options.label: British English
options.description: e.g. en-GB-RyanNeural / SoniaNeural.

options.label: Nigerian English
options.description: en-NG-AbeoNeural / EzinneNeural (+ en-KE Chilemba / Asilia as a second pair).

options.label: Other language
options.description: Tell me the language/region; I'll list matching voices to audition.

options.label: One narrator
options.description: Same voice on every video. Simple and consistent.

options.label: One per series
options.description: Each audience/track gets its own narrator (e.g. members vs admins).

options.label: Narrator + dialogue
options.description: Main narrator plus two-voice role-play scenes (e.g. a buyer and a seller).

options.label: Formal but simple
options.description: Short sentences, plain words, no slang. Works for every audience.

options.label: Friendly & casual
options.description: Conversational, 'you'll love this', light humour.

options.label: Professional
options.description: Corporate/B2B, precise, outcome-focused.

questions.question: Where will the videos go? (pick all)

options.label: YouTube
options.description: Full SEO pack: titles, descriptions, chapters, tags, thumbnails, playlists (vidIQ connector or Studio).

options.label: Inside the product/site
options.description: Embedded in the app or docs (YouTube embed or self-hosted MP4).

options.label: Social
options.description: Vertical cut-downs for Shorts / Reels / TikTok / LinkedIn.

options.label: Just the files
options.description: MP4s in out/final; I'll handle distribution.

options.label: Intro + outro
options.description: 5.5s logo-tile intro with the episode title, 7s logo signature outro with tagline + URL.

options.label: Intro only
options.description: Title intro, no outro (shorter).

options.label: None
options.description: Straight in (best for Shorts and in-app clips); logo bug stays in the corner.

questions.question: Background music? (picked to fit this project's sound brief)

options.label: Upbeat
options.description: Driving, positive bed matched to the project's sound brief, fetched from free open sources (Openverse CC0/CC-BY, Freesound); ducked under speech. Credits are added to descriptions automatically.

options.label: Calm
options.description: Soft ambient/piano bed from free open sources, chosen to fit the project; credits handled automatically.

options.label: Playful
options.description: Bouncy, light bed (ukulele, whistle, pizzicato) from free open sources; credits handled automatically.

options.label: None
options.description: Voice and sound effects only.

questions.question: How much do you want to review?

options.label: Approve each script
options.description: I write every script, you approve it, then I build. Plus a stills check before each render.

options.label: Approve per batch
options.description: Approve the video list + all scripts of a batch at once, then I build the batch.

options.label: Autopilot
options.description: I plan, script, build and render; you review the finished videos.

presenter-character.question: What should the presenter look like?
presenter-character.note: Render the PresenterDemo composition as a still and show it; ask skin tone, hair style (short | afro | bun | long | bald), outfit colour (default brand primary), side (left | right). Save to video.config.json → presenter.

real-presenter.question: Real person or AI avatar?
real-presenter.note: Options: 'I'll record myself' (clips in public/presenter/, layout bubble | side | full) or 'AI avatar' (HeyGen / D-ID: needs HEYGEN_API_KEY or DID_API_KEY in ~/.video-studio/secrets.env; generate one clip per line from the script, then place with <TalkingHead>).

accent:other.question: Which language and region?
accent:other.note: List 4–6 matching Azure voices (or ElevenLabs voices), render a 1-line sample of each to out/voice-samples/, and let the user rank them.

_agents: No multiple-choice question tool (e.g. a non-Claude agent, or plain chat)? Ask each round as a numbered list in chat — questions 1-4, options a-d — and accept short answers like "1b 2a 3c 4a" (several letters for multi-select, or free text for Other). Without any agent, run `node <skill>/scripts/setup.mjs` for the same questions in the terminal.
